Consequence: a role relaunched within 60 s of the stop logs `skipped: another process holds` and keeps the partial index; one after 60 s takes over (clone4's 9-minute-old lease was repaired to complete in 59.6 s). The test accepts a shim that returns only once an in-flight warm-up has returned (its codegraph child dead with the group, its release run), bounded (the test allows 10 s; the launcher's StopGrace is 30 s), with the agent's exit status kept; the codegraph.go comment then needs to say what actually guarantees the release.

observations: `--no-extensions` never fenced a repository's `.omp/skills`, `.claude/skills` or `.mcp.json`: with the flag inserted into the branch's argv both tester skills and the MCP tool were still listed. The spec's problem statement overstates the fence; what the flag held off was the repository's extensions (and hooks/commands, per the rewritten sandbox test) and the profile's plugins, pi-codegraph among them.

dev.autoqa defaults to true on the pinned fork once PI_AUTO_QA=0 leaves the baseline (dev.autoqaConsent = unset, push endpoint https://qa.omp.sh/v1/grievances): a pod now has an Oh My Pi default that posts tool-issue reports outward unless the operator's overlay sets dev.autoqa: false. The implementation follows the spec (the two environment defaults go); whether the operator overlay should pin it is the architect's and operator's call, already reported by the implementer.

The lease left behind by a group SIGTERM is bounded by the design's own stale takeover: a relaunch after 60 s repairs the index (measured 59.6 s on a 9-minute-old lease over a partial index). The failure is the relaunch within that minute and the wrong claim in codegraph.go about what guarantees the release.
